HP has a lion's share of the market, and they've been producing extremely low quality cartridges that are more or less designed to fail. They've also shifted to cartridges that seem cheap, but have very low levels of ink, so your price per unit is very high. Cost per mL was about 75 cents or so with the old HP 45 cartridges, but they're around $40 retail. HP 61 cartridges are around $2.65 per mL, but they're only like $15 off the shelf. Consumers are generally only looking at the basic price, not price per mL. Also, newer versions of Windows are also not compatible with the older printers that took more economical cartridges.

With empty cores of 61's having an IMMENSE rate of failure, and being high cost of $3-$5 per EMPTY cartridge, it's really putting a hurt on stores like where I work. As well, there is always going to be a group of people who look to save even more money once they find out that they can save any. We've lost several customers to Chinese import cartridges on eBay and Amazon.

I do what I can to keep costs down at work, and do right by my customers, but the end is nigh. 300 some odd locations closed down in the past year. One other location we speak with often has gone from $35-$40k in sales per month down to $12-$15k.
